import html # A simple HTML template for a blog post. The placeholders are used by str.format(). BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def format_blog_entry(headline: str, content: str) -> str: """ Prepare a blog entry for safe web display. Parameters ---------- headline : str The main heading or subject of the blog post. content : str The complete textual content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A sanitized and HTML‑formatted string ready to be embedded in a web page. Notes ----- * The function uses :func:`html.escape` to neutralise any characters that could otherwise be interpreted as HTML, preventing injection attacks (CWE‑74). * The returned string contains the supplied headline and content substituted into :data:`BLOG_FORMAT`. """ # Ensure both arguments are strings; if not, convert them. headline = str(headline) content = str(content) # Escape special HTML characters to prevent injection. safe_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_content = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Build the final HTML using the template. formatted_post = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_headline, body=safe_content) return formatted_post
